question: An HIV-positive patient has a CD4+ count of 180 cells/μL and presents with dry cough, progressive dyspnoea, and bilateral interstitial infiltrates on chest X-ray. Which opportunistic infection is MOST likely at this CD4 threshold?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. PCP typically occurs when CD4+ drops below 200 cells/μL (the AIDS-defining threshold). It presents with dry cough, progressive dyspnoea, and bilateral interstitial or ground-glass infiltrates. Diagnosis is by GMS stain of induced sputum or BAL. Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis is recommended when CD4 < 200.

Incorrect. CMV retinitis typically occurs at CD4 < 50 cells/μL — much lower than this patient's count — and presents with visual disturbances (floaters, visual field defects), not respiratory symptoms.

Incorrect. Disseminated MAC typically occurs at CD4 < 50 cells/μL with fever, weight loss, anaemia, and hepatosplenomegaly. At CD4 180, the respiratory picture with bilateral infiltrates is more consistent with PCP (threshold: <200).

Incorrect. Herpes zoster can occur at relatively higher CD4 counts (200–500) and presents as a painful vesicular rash in a dermatomal distribution, not as bilateral pulmonary infiltrates with dyspnoea.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key OI thresholds: 200–500 (TB, oral candidiasis, herpes zoster); <200 — AIDS threshold (PCP, Toxoplasma encephalitis, Cryptococcal meningitis); <50 (CMV retinitis, disseminated MAC). This patient's respiratory presentation at CD4 180 fits PCP.
Correct! PCP is the most common AIDS-defining illness and occurs at CD4 < 200. Remember: 200–500 (TB, candidiasis, zoster) → <200 (PCP, Toxoplasma, Cryptococcus) → <50 (CMV, MAC).
